results.change_intent: Prevent recursive command buffer submission during memory defragmentation and texture cycling by appending defrag work directly to the submitted command buffer and deferring cleanups to presentation submits.
results.summary: Fixes recursive submission during defragmentation by passing the active command buffer into defrag and texture cycling routines; however, the `defragInProgress` flag is left asserted when defrag finishes or fails.

issues.comment: renderer->defragInProgress is set to 1 at the beginning of VULKAN_INTERNAL_DefragmentMemory, but it is never reset back to 0 on any return path (neither on allocation failure nor on successful completion). Because VULKAN_Submit checks '!renderer->defragInProgress' before calling defragmentation, defragmentation will run at most once during the renderer's entire lifetime and will permanently block subsequent defragmentations.
issues.suggestion: Reset renderer->defragInProgress = 0 when VULKAN_INTERNAL_DefragmentMemory exits, both before returning false on error and before returning true at the end of the function.

issues.evidence:
texture = VULKAN_INTERNAL_CreateTexture(
        renderer,
        false,
        &container->header.info);

    VULKAN_INTERNAL_TextureTransitionToDefaultUsage(
        renderer,
        commandBuffer,
        VULKAN_TEXTURE_USAGE_MODE_UNINITIALIZED,
        texture);
issues.comment: In VULKAN_INTERNAL_CycleActiveTexture, VULKAN_INTERNAL_TextureTransitionToDefaultUsage is called with texture before checking if texture is NULL. If VULKAN_INTERNAL_CreateTexture fails (for example due to out-of-memory), texture will be NULL, causing a null pointer dereference inside VULKAN_INTERNAL_TextureTransitionToDefaultUsage.
issues.suggestion: Move the null check for texture to occur immediately after VULKAN_INTERNAL_CreateTexture returns, before invoking VULKAN_INTERNAL_TextureTransitionToDefaultUsage.

issues.comment: The error message says 'Failed to allocate defrag buffer!' in the texture creation failure path.
issues.suggestion: Update the log message to 'Failed to allocate defrag texture!' to distinguish it from buffer allocation failures.
